title: Dedicated throughput SLO + tier definitions (Standard/Plus/Premium) — v1 initiative
creator: Lauren Bishop
description:
Goal: Make Dedicated purchases predictable by shipping a formal throughput SLO definition + a tier taxonomy (Standard/Plus/Premium) mapped to standardized hardware shapes + pricing tiers. This is the umbrella initiative to coordinate Product, SRE, Infra/Fleet, Observability, Finance, Legal, Sales Enablement, Support/CS.

Why now:
- Dedicated deals (and renewals) are stalling on “what is guaranteed?” and “how do we measure it?”
- Current Dedicated sizing is ad-hoc by region/hardware availability; guarantees are inconsistent and hard to support operationally.
- We need tier-aware routing/admission control to protect guaranteed customers under fleet contention.

What we will ship (v1):
1) Dedicated throughput SLO (customer-facing commitments + internal SLO semantics)
- Canonical metric definition (tokens/sec attribution model, streaming semantics, measurement window)
- Exclusions (customer-side throttling/backpressure, unsupported model/version, customer-configured max_concurrency, misuse patterns)
- Model/version constraints and “pinned version” behavior
- Warm pool / cold start behavior and what counts toward SLO
- Reporting and remedy hooks (credit policy integration handled via Support/CS + Legal)

2) Tier taxonomy (Standard / Plus / Premium)
- Entitlements per tier: throughput floor, burst policy, failover posture, support response targets
- Operational behavior: tier-aware routing, overload shedding rules, burst pool usage, admission control

3) Hardware shape catalog (standardized)
- Per region: GPU type/count, CPU/RAM, networking, storage; supported model families; max context + batching recommendations
- Baseline perf profiles with expected variance and how we use them for commitments

4) Pricing/packaging mapping
- Tier → shape(s) → list price guidance and discount guardrails
- Margin assumptions validated by Finance/FP&A; deal desk triggers

5) Operationalization
- Dashboards (per-customer throughput floor tracking), burn-rate alerting, and SLO reporting
- Runbooks and escalation playbooks (SRE/Infra/Support)

Non-goals (v1):
- A universal, model-agnostic TPS guarantee across all models and future versions without pinning (we will scope to supported model/version sets per tier/shape)
- Auto-provisioning any arbitrary shape requested by customers (we will standardize and allow exceptions via deal desk)
- Perfect apples-to-apples comparison vs Hosted API performance (we will provide guidance but not promise Hosted parity)

Milestones / target dates (subject to supply + metric sign-off):
- M0: Metric decision + ADR sign-off (target: 2025-02-07)
  - Exit: canonical throughput metric selected; known pitfalls documented (streaming tokens, batching, caching)
- M1: Draft SLO + exclusions + remedies hooks (target: 2025-02-21)
  - Exit: SRE + Legal + CS alignment on customer-facing language and internal semantics
- M2: Tier definitions v1 (Standard/Plus/Premium) (target: 2025-03-01)
  - Exit: throughput floor policy, burst policy, failover posture, support response targets agreed
- M3: Shape catalog + tier→shape mapping per region (target: 2025-03-15)
  - Exit: standard shapes published for top 3 regions; model/version constraints defined
- M4: Pricing bands + discount guardrails (target: 2025-03-29)
  - Exit: Finance-approved list price guidance and GM floors; deal desk triggers defined
- M5: Implementation complete (target: 2025-04-19)
  - Exit: metrics shipped; tier-aware routing/admission control on; dashboards/alerts live; burst metering exporting
- M6: Limited GA (5–8 beta Dedicated customers) (target: 2025-05-10)
  - Exit: signed SLO terms where applicable; operational readiness; retro plan scheduled

Launch criteria (limited GA):
- SLO definition is unambiguous and not easily gameable
  - Streaming token accounting verified (no double-counting)
  - Measurement windows + attribution documented (per-deployment; tagged by deployment_id/model/region)
  - Exclusions list reviewed by Legal + Support (customer backpressure, customer config, unsupported models/versions)
- Tier enforcement works under contention
  - Tier-aware admission control enabled and validated via load tests
  - Routing policy maps tier→pool/shape with safe fallback behavior
- Reporting + operations are ready
  - Dashboard shows: throughput floor, saturation signals, burn-rate, recent incidents
  - Alerting tuned to avoid noise; oncall routing set
  - Escalation runbooks + credit hooks exist and are used in tabletop exercise
- Commercial enablement is complete
  - Cheat sheet reviewed by Sales + CS; quoting guardrails in place
  - Contract/order form language approved for tiers that include written commitments

Primary risks / open questions:
- Model-dependent TPS variance and customer prompt mix: mitigate via supported model sets + pinned versions + stated confidence bands
- Regional GPU supply heterogeneity: mitigate via region-specific shape catalogs and explicit lead times; avoid bespoke shapes by default
- Metric pitfalls: streaming, batching, caching, and warmup can cause misleading TPS; mitigate with canonical instrumentation and a single source of truth dashboard
- SLO that’s too strict → operational burden; too loose → customer distrust: mitigate via limited GA + retro + adjust tier thresholds
